cues.en: All right, let's get started. This is 6824, distributed systems. So I'd like to start with just a brief explanation of what I think a distributed system is. The core of it is a set of cooperating computers that are communicating with each other over networked to get some coherent tasks done. And so the kinds of examples.
cues.zh: 好了，我们开始吧。这是 6.824，分布式系统课程。我想先简单解释一下我心目中的分布式系统是什么。它的核心是一组相互协作的计算机，它们通过网络相互通信，共同完成某个一致的任务。至于我们会关注的例子嘛。

cues.en: that we'll be focusing on in this class are things like storage for big websites, or big data computations such as MapReduce, and also somewhat more exotic things like peer-to-peer file sharing. So those are all just examples of kinds of case studies we'll look at. And the reason why all this is important is that a lot of critical infrastructure out there is built out of distributed systems.
cues.zh: 本课程重点讨论的例子包括大型网站的存储系统，或者像 MapReduce 这样的大数据计算，还有一些比较特别的东西，比如点对点文件共享。这些都只是我们要研究的案例类型中的一些例子。为什么这些内容很重要呢？因为如今很多关键的基础设施都是由分布式系统构建的。

cues.en: infrastructure that requires more than one computer to get its job done, or it sort of inherently needs to be spread out physically. So the reasons why people build this stuff, first of all, before I even talk about distributed systems, I just want to remind you that if you're designing a system, you're designing, you need to solve some problem. If you can possibly solve it on a single computer without building a distributed system, you should do it that way.
cues.zh: 这些基础设施要么需要不止一台计算机才能完成工作，要么天然就需要在物理上分散部署。人们构建这些东西的原因，首先，在讲分布式系统之前，我只是想提醒你，如果你在设计一个系统，你需要解决某个问题。如果可以在单台计算机上解决，而不必构建分布式系统，那你就应该那样做。

cues.en: And there's many, many jobs you can get done on a single computer, and it's always easier. So distributed systems, you should try everything else before you try building distributed systems, because they're not simpler. So the reason why people are driven to use lots of cooperating computers are they need to get high performance. And the way to think about that is they want to achieve some sort of parallelism.
cues.zh: 很多任务在单台计算机上就能完成，而且总是更简单。所以对于分布式系统，你应该先尝试所有其他方案，再考虑构建分布式系统，因为它们并不简单。那么，人们被迫使用大量协作计算机的原因是什么呢？首先，他们需要高性能。可以这样理解，他们想实现某种程度的并行。

cues.en: Lots of CPUs, lots of memories, lots of disk arms moving in parallel. Another reason why people build this stuff is to be able to tolerate faults. Have two computers do the exact same thing. If one of them fails, you can cut over to the other one. Another is that some problems are just naturally spread out in space. Like, you know, you want to do interbank transfers of money or something. Well, you know, bank A has this computer in New York City and bank B has this computer in London, you know.
cues.zh: 大量的 CPU、大量的内存、大量的磁盘臂并行工作。人们构建分布式系统的另一个原因是容错。让两台计算机做完全相同的事情，如果一台出了故障，你就可以切换到另一台。还有一个原因是，有些问题天然在空间上是分散的。比如，你想做银行间的转账。嗯，你知道，银行 A 在纽约有一台计算机，银行 B 在伦敦有一台计算机。

cues.en: You just have to have some way for them to talk to each other and cooperate in order to carry that out. So there's some natural sort of physical reasons, systems that are inherently physically distributed. The final reason that people build this stuff is in order to achieve some sort of security goal. So often by if there's some code you don't trust or you need to interact with somebody but they may be malicious or maybe their code has bugs in it.
cues.zh: 那你就必须有某种方式让它们相互通信、相互协作，才能完成这项工作。所以存在一些天然的物理原因，有些系统本身就分布在物理上不同的位置。人们构建分布式系统的最后一个原因是为了实现某种安全目标。通常，如果有一些你不信任的代码，或者你需要与某人交互，但对方可能有恶意，或者他们的代码可能存在 bug。

cues.en: So you don't want to have to trust it. You may want to split up the computation. So your stuff runs over there. And that computer and my stuff runs here on this computer. And they only talk to each other through some sort of narrowly defined network protocol. So we may be worried about security. And that's achieved by splitting things up into multiple computers so that they can be isolated. Most of this course is going to be about performance and fault tolerance, although the other two
cues.zh: 所以你并不想完全信任它。你可能会想把计算拆分开。这样你的任务跑在那台机器上，而我的任务跑在这台电脑上。它们之间仅通过某种严格定义的网络协议进行通信。所以我们可能会担心安全性。而通过把任务拆分到多台计算机上，就能实现相互隔离。本门课程大部分内容会聚焦于性能和容错，尽管另外两个因素

cues.en: will often work themselves in by way of the sort of constraints on the case studies that we're going to look at. Another thing that makes distributed systems hard is that
cues.zh: 也常常会作为约束条件，体现在我们要探讨的案例分析中。大家知道，分布式系统之所以存在这些问题，是因为它们包含很多部件，而且由于有多台计算机，这些部件都是并发执行的。你会遇到并发编程带来的所有麻烦，各种复杂的交互以及诡异的时序依赖问题。这也是分布式系统之所以困难的原因之一。另一个让分布式系统变得棘手的是，

cues.en: Because again, you have multiple pieces plus a network, you can have very unexpected failure patterns. That is, if you have a single computer, it's usually the case either the computer works, or maybe it crashes or suffers a power failure or something. But it pretty much either works or doesn't work. Distributed systems made up of lots of computers, you can have partial failures. That is, some pieces stop working, other pieces continue working. Or maybe the computers are working, but some part of the network.
cues.zh: 同样因为系统由多个组件加上网络构成，可能会出现极难预料的故障模式。也就是说，如果只有单台计算机，情况通常要么是它正常运行，要么是宕机或断电之类的。基本非黑即白，要么工作要么挂掉。而由多台机器构成的分布式系统，则可能发生部分失效。也就是说，一部分组件停止工作，另一部分还在继续运转。或者计算机本身工作正常，但网络的某一部分

cues.en: is broken or unreliable. So partial failures is another reason why distributed systems are hard. This is sort of basic challenges. A final reason why it's hard is that the original reason to build a distributed system is often to get higher performance, to get 1,000 computers worth of performance or 1,000 disk arms worth of performance. But it's actually very tricky to obtain that.
cues.zh: 出现故障或不可靠。因此，部分失效是分布式系统难做的另一个原因。这些都属于基础挑战。最后一个难点在于，构建分布式系统的初衷往往是为了获取更高的性能，比如发挥出 1000 台计算机的性能，或 1000 个磁盘磁头的性能。但想要真正达成这点其实非常困难。

cues.en: 1,000x speed up with 1,000 computers. There's often a lot of roadblocks thrown in your way. And what I mean by scalability or scalable speed up is that
cues.zh: 这些是构建分布式系统时需要用到的关键工具。另一个在我们要讨论的所有论文中都会出现的大主题是性能。通常，构建分布式系统的高层目标就是获得人们所说的可扩展的加速比。所以我们会关注可扩展性。我所说的可扩展性或可扩展加速比是指：

cues.en: If I have some problem that I'm solving with one computer and I buy a second computer to help me execute my problem, if I can now solve the problem in half the time or maybe solve twice as many problem instances per minute on two computers as I had on one, then that's an example of scalability. cues.zh: 如果我有一个问题，用一台计算机来求解，然后我买了第二台计算机来帮我执行这个问题，如果我现在能用一半的时间求解，或者说每分钟能求解的问题实例数量是原来一台时的两倍，这就是可扩展性的一个例子。也就是说，两倍的计算机或资源能带来……

cues.en: two times the performance or throughput. And this is a huge hammer. If you can build a system that actually has this behavior, namely that if you increase the number of computers, you throw at the problem by some factor, you get that factor, more throughput, more performance out of the system. That's a huge win because you can buy computers with just money. Whereas if in order to get the alternative to this is that
cues.zh: 两倍的性能或吞吐量。这是个巨大的利器。如果你能构建一个真正具备这种特性的系统，也就是说，你把投入解决问题的计算机数量增加某个倍数，就能从系统中获得同样倍数的吞吐量和性能。那就是巨大的胜利，因为计算机用钱就能买到。而另一种选择是——

cues.en: In order to get more performance, you have to pay programmers to restructure your software to get better performance, to make it more efficient, or to apply some sort of specialized techniques, better algorithms or something. cues.zh: 为了获得更高性能，你得花钱请程序员重构软件，以提升性能、提高效率，或者采用某种专门技术、更好的算法之类的东西。如果你必须花钱请程序员修改代码让它更快，那是一种昂贵的方式。我们当然希望能直接买 1,000 台计算机而不是 10 台，就获得 100 倍的吞吐量。那太棒了。所以这种可扩展性思路是一个巨大的

cues.zh: 当人们构建大型网站之类、让它们运行在装满计算机的大楼里时，这种想法就在他们脑海深处。如果那栋装满计算机的大楼就是为了获得某种相应规模的性能。但你必须小心设计，才能真正获得那种性能。所以在本课程中，我们看架构图或画架构图时，这种情况通常是这样：假设我们在构建一个网站。

cues.en: web server and a computer from the database, but maybe all of a sudden you get really popular and you, you know, 100 million people sign up for your service. cues.zh: 买更多 Web 服务器，然后把用户分流，让一半用户或一部分用户去 Web 服务器一，另一半送到 Web 服务器二。因为也许你在构建，我不知道，Reddit 之类的东西，最终所有用户都需要看到相同的数据，所以你让所有 Web 服务器都与后端通信。也许在这里你可以持续增加 Web 服务器很长时间。所以这就是一种让 Web 服务器代码获得并行加速的方法。

cues.en: If you're running PHP or Python, maybe it's not too efficient. As long as each individual web server doesn't put too much load on the database, you can add a lot of web servers before you run into problems. And so what tends to happen with these systems is that at some point after you have 10 or 20 or 100 web servers all talking to the same database,
cues.zh: 如果你用的是 PHP 或 Python，也许效率不太高。但只要每台 Web 服务器对数据库的压力不太大，你就可以加很多台服务器才出问题。可惜这种扩展性很少是无限的。不经过深思熟虑肯定做不到。所以这类系统通常的情况是：当你有了 10 台、20 台或 100 台 Web 服务器都连着同一个数据库之后，到了某个时候，

So it's rare that you get full scalability through sort of infinite numbers of adding infinite numbers of computers. The thing is limiting performance from the web servers to the database. And at this point...
cues.zh: 现在突然之间，数据库开始成为瓶颈，再增加 Web 服务器也无济于事了。所以，你很难通过无休止地堆机器来获得完全的可扩展性。到了一定程度这种做法就失效了，因为你增加机器的地方已经不再是瓶颈所在。部署了大量的 Web 服务器，我们其实只是转移了瓶颈。限制性能的瓶颈从 Web 服务器转移到了数据库。而在这个时候……

cues.en: actually you almost certainly have to do a bit of design work because it's rare that you can take that there's any straightforward way to take a single database and Sort of refactor things with it for you can take Data sorted in a single database and refactor it. cues.zh: 实际上你几乎肯定得做一些设计上的工作，因为很少有直接了当的办法，能把存储在单个数据库里的数据直接重构，比如把它拆分到多个数据库里。这往往工作量不小，而且也挺麻烦的，但确实有很多人实际需要这么做。

cues.en: push this idea infinitely far. Okay, so another big topic that comes up a lot is fault tolerance. If you're building a system with a single computer in it, well, a single computer often can stay up for years. Like, I have servers in my office that have been up for years without crashing. You know, the computer's pretty reliable, the operating system's pretty reliable.
cues.zh: 把这个想法无限推演下去。好，另一个经常出现的大话题是容错。如果你构建的系统里只有一台计算机，那么单台计算机通常能连续运行好几年。比如，我办公室里的服务器已经连续运行好几年都没崩过。你知道，计算机相当可靠，操作系统也相当可靠。

cues.en: Apparently the power in my building is pretty reliable. So it's not uncommon to have single computers. They just stay up for amazing amounts of time. However, if you're building systems out of thousands of computers, then even if each computer can be expected to stay up for a year, with 1,000 computers, that means you're going to have about three computer failures per day in your set of 1,000 computers. So solving big problems with big distributed systems turns sort of
cues.zh: 看来我所在大楼的供电相当稳定，所以单台计算机连续运行很长时间并不稀奇。不过，如果你用成千上万台计算机构建系统，即使每台计算机平均能运行一年，拥有 1,000 台计算机也意味着每天大约会有三台发生故障。所以，用大型分布式系统解决大型问题，事情就变得有点】【。

cues.en: very rare fault tolerance, very rare failure, very rare failure problems into failure problems that happen just all the time. cues.zh: 把极少见的容错问题、极少见的故障，变成几乎一直都会发生的故障问题。在一个拥有 1,000 台计算机的系统中，几乎可以肯定总有某些东西出了问题。总有一台计算机要么崩溃了，要么不知怎么回事，运行不正常、速度变慢，或者执行了错误的操作。也可能是网络的某个部分出了问题。毕竟有 1,000 台计算机，我们就会有大量网线和大量网络交换机。所以……

cues.en: There's always some network cable that somebody stepped on and is unreliability, or network cable that fell out, or some network switch whose fan is broken and the switch overheated and failed. cues.zh:
总会有某根网线被人踩到、变得不可靠，或者网线松脱，或者某个网络交换机的风扇坏了，交换机过热而故障。
在你的楼宇级分布式系统里，总会有某个小地方出问题。

这意味着……

cues.en: Failure has to be really, or the response, the masking of failures, the ability to proceed without failures just has to be built into the design, because there's always failures. And as part of building convenient abstractions for application programmers, we really need to be able to build infrastructure that as much as possible hides the failures from application programmers or masks them or something so that every application programmer doesn't have to have a
cues.zh: 故障应对、故障屏蔽，以及在故障下继续运行的能力，必须直接内置在设计之中，因为故障总是不可避免的。而为了给应用开发者提供便利的抽象，我们确实需要构建出尽可能对他们隐藏或屏蔽故障的基础设施，这样每个应用开发者就用不着去……

cues.en: complete complicated story for all the different kinds of failures that can occur. cues.zh: 针对可能发生的各种故障，情况非常复杂。对于什么是容错，以及它的确切含义，有很多不同的理解。我们会看到很多不同的形式，但其中最常见的一个概念就是可用性。因此，有些系统的设计目标就是在……

cues.en: certain kinds of failures, not all failures, but certain kinds of failures, the system will keep operating despite the failure while providing undamaged service, the same kind of service it would have provided even if there had been no failure. cues.zh: 某些类型的故障——不是所有故障，而是某些类型的故障——即使发生了故障，系统仍能继续运行，并提供未受损的服务，和没有发生故障时一样的服务。所以有些系统在这个意义上是可用的。假设你构建了一个复制服务，它可能有两个副本，如果其中一个副本服务器挂了，

cues.en: fails, maybe the other server can continue operating. They both fail, of course. You can't promise availability in that case. So available systems usually say, well, under a certain set of failures, we're going to continue providing service. We're going to be available. If more failures than that occur, it won't be available anymore. Another kind of fault tolerance you might have, or in addition to availability, or by itself, is recoverability.
cues.zh: 发生故障时，也许另一台服务器还能继续运行。当然，它们也可能同时故障。这种情况下，你就无法保证服务可用。所以，可用系统通常会说：在特定故障范围内，我们会继续提供服务，保持可用；如果故障超出这个范围，服务就不再可用了。除了可用性之外，或者单独作为一种能力，另一种容错能力是可恢复性。

cues.en: And what this means is that if something goes wrong, maybe the service will stop working. That is, it'll simply stop responding to requests. And it'll wait for someone to come along and repair whatever went wrong. But after the repair occurs, the system will be able to continue as if nothing bad had gone wrong. So this is sort of a weaker requirement than availability, because here we're not going to do anything until the failed component has been repaired. But the fact that we can get up
cues.zh: 这意味着，如果出了问题，服务可能会停止工作，也就是干脆不再响应请求，然后等待有人来修复故障。但修复完成之后，系统就能继续运行，就好像什么坏事都没发生过一样。所以这算是比可用性更弱的一个要求，因为在这里，故障组件修复之前我们什么都不做。但关键是，我们能够重新站起来

cues.en: get going again without any loss of correctness is still a significant requirement. It means recoverable systems typically need to do things like save their latest data on disk or something where they can get it back after the power comes back up. And even among available systems, in order for a system to be useful in real life, usually the way available systems are specced is that
cues.zh: 在保证正确性的前提下重新恢复运行，仍然是一个很高的要求。这意味着可恢复系统通常需要把最新数据保存到磁盘，或某种在重新通电后能找回数据的地方。而且即使在可用系统中，为了让系统在现实中具有实用价值，通常对可用系统的规范要求是

cues.en: They're available until some number of failures have happened. If too many failures have happened, an available system will stop working, or will stop responding at all, but when enough things have been repaired, it'll continue operating. So a good available system will sort of be recoverable as well, in the sense that if too many failures occur, it'll stop answering, but then we'll continue correctly after that.
cues.zh: 在发生一定数量的故障之前，它们都是可用的。如果故障发生得太多，可用系统就会停止工作，或者彻底停止响应，但在修复了足够多的故障之后，它又会继续运行。所以一个优秀的可用系统在某种程度上也具备可恢复性，也就是说，如果发生过多故障，它会停止响应，但在那之后仍能正确地继续运行。

cues.en: So this is what we'd love to, this is what we'd love to obtain. The biggest hammer, we'll see a number of approaches to solving these problems. There's really sort of two things that are the most important tools we have in this department. One is non-volatile storage. So that, you know, if something crashes, power fails or whatever. Maybe there's a building wide power failure. We can use non-volatile storage like.
cues.zh: 这就是我们非常想要达到的，这就是我们想要获得的结果。最有力的工具，我们会看到多种解决这些问题的方法。这个领域里真正最重要的工具其实有两样。一个是非易失性存储。这样，你知道，如果什么东西崩溃了、断电了或者别的什么，也许是整栋楼断电。我们可以用非易失性存储，比如……

cues.en: hard drives or flash or solid-state drives or something to sort of store a checkpoint or a log of the state of the system. And then when the power comes back up or somebody repairs our power supply or who knows what, we'll be able to read our latest state off the hard drive and continue from there. So one tool is sort of non-volatile storage and.
cues.zh: 硬盘、闪存或固态硬盘之类的东西，来存储检查点或系统状态日志。然后当电力恢复、有人修好了电源，或者谁知道怎样，我们就能从硬盘读取最新状态，并从那里继续。所以一种工具就是非易失性存储，以及……

cues.en: The management of non-volatile storage doesn't think it comes up a lot because non-volatile storage tends to be expensive to update. And so a huge amount of the sort of nitty gritty of building sort of high performance fault tolerant systems is in clever ways to avoid having to write the non-volatile storage too much. In the old days, and even today, what writing non-volatile storage meant was moving a disk arm and waiting for a disk platter to rotate.
cues.zh: 非易失性存储的管理，我不觉得会经常被提到，因为非易失性存储更新起来往往很贵。所以构建高性能容错系统的大量琐碎细节，都在于用巧妙的方法避免过多写入非易失性存储。过去乃至今天，写入非易失性存储意味着移动磁盘臂，并等待盘片旋转。

cues.en: Both of which are agonizingly slow on the scale of three gigahertz microprocessors. With things like flash, life's quite a bit better, but still requires a lot of thought to get good performance out of. And the other big tool we have for fault tolerance is replication. And the management of replicated copies is sort of tricky, that sort of key.
cues.zh: 相对于三吉赫兹微处理器的速度，这两者都慢得令人痛苦。用闪存之类的东西，情况会好不少，但仍要花很多心思才能获得好性能。容错的另一个重要工具是复制。而副本管理有点棘手，算是一个关键点。

cues.en: problem lurking in any replicated system where we have two servers each with a supposedly identical copy of the system state. The key problem that comes up is always that the two replicas will accidentally drift out of sync and will stop being replicas. And this is just with the back of every design that we're going to see for using replication to get fault tolerance. And lab two and lab three are all about management of
cues.zh: 关键问题潜伏在任何复制系统中：我们有两台服务器，各自持有一份据称完全相同的系统状态副本。真正出现的关键问题总是，两个副本会意外失去同步，不再成其为副本。这正是我们即将看到的每一个用复制实现容错的设计背后的隐患。而 lab two 和 lab three 全都是关于……的管理

So as an example of what I mean by consistency, supposing we're building a distributed storage system and it's a key value service. So it just supports two operations. Maybe there's a put operation and you give it a key and a value and it...
cues.zh: 用于容错的副本。你会看到，这相当复杂。最后一个主题，最后一个贯穿性主题，是一致性。举个例子说明我所说的一致性：假设我们在构建一个分布式存储系统，它是一个键值服务。它只支持两个操作。也许有一个 put 操作，你给它一个键和一个值，它……

The client sends a key and the storage service is supposed to respond with the value to store it for that key. And this is kind of the, when I can't think of anything else as an example of the distributed system, I'll whip out key value services.
cues.zh: 存储系统就把这个值收起来，作为这个键对应的值。所以它维护的就是一张大的键值表。然后还有一个 get 操作。客户端发送一个键，存储服务应当返回为该键存储的值。这有点像，每当我想不出分布式系统的其他例子时，我就会搬出键值服务来举例。

cues.en: I mean, they're very useful, right? They're just sort of the kind of fundamental, simple version of a storage system. So, of course, if you're an application programmer, it's helpful if these two operations kind of have meanings attached to them that you can go look in the manual and the manual says, you know, what it means, what you'll get back if you call get, right? And sort of what it means for you to call put.
cues.zh: 我是说，它们非常有用，对吧？它们差不多就是存储系统最基本、最简单的版本。所以，当然，如果你是应用开发者，如果这两个操作带有明确的含义会很有帮助：你可以去查手册，手册会说明它是什么意思，调用 get 会返回什么，对吧？以及调用 put 意味着什么。

cues.en: So it's great if there's some sort of spec for what they meant. Otherwise, who knows? How can you possibly write an application without a description of what putting get are supposed to do? And this is the topic of consistency. And the reason why it's interesting in distributed systems is that both for performance and for fault tolerant reasons, fault tolerance reasons, we often have more than one copy of the data floating around. So in a non-distributed system where you just have
cues.zh: 所以，如果能有某种规范说明它们的含义，那就很好。否则，谁知道呢？如果没有描述 put 和 get 应该做什么，你怎么可能写出应用？这就是一致性的主题。它在分布式系统中有趣的原因是，无论出于性能还是容错原因、容错原因，我们经常会有不止一份数据副本在四处存在。所以在非分布式系统中，你只有

cues.en: a single server with a single table, there's often, although not always, but there's often relatively no ambiguity about what put and get could possibly mean, right? Intuitively, what put means is update the table, and what get means is just get me the version that's stored in the table. But in a distributed system where there's more than one copy of the data due to replication or caching or who knows what, there may be lots of different versions
cues.zh: 一台服务器和一张表时，对于 put 和 get 可能是什么意思，通常——虽然不是总是——通常相对没有歧义，对吧？直观地说，put 的意思是更新表，get 的意思就是把表里存的那一版拿给我。但在分布式系统中，由于复制、缓存或天知道什么原因，数据会有不止一份副本，于是可能存在许多不同的版本

cues.en: Of this key value pair floating around like if one of the replicas, you know, supposing some client issues are put and You know, there's two copies of the the server So they both have a key value table Right and maybe key one has value 20 on both of them and then some client issues are put As we have a client over here and it's going to send a put it wants to update the value of one to be
cues.zh: 这个键值对在四处存在。比如，假设其中一个副本，假设某个客户端发出一个 put，你知道，服务器有两份副本，所以它们都有一张键值表，对吧？也许键 1 在两边的值都是 20，然后某个客户端发出一个 put。假设这边有个客户端，它要发送一个 put，想把键 1 的值更新为

cues.en: 21, right, maybe it's counting stuff in this key value server. So it sends a put with key one and value 21. It sends it to the first server and it's about to send the same put, you know, it wants to update both copies, right, to keep them in sync. It's about to send this put, but just before it sends the put to the second server, it crashes, right, power failure or bug and operating system or something. So now the state we're left in, sadly, is that we sent this put and so we've updated one
cues.zh: 21，对吧，也许它在这个键值服务器里做计数。于是它发送一个带键 1 和值 21 的 put。它把 put 发给第一台服务器，然后正准备发送同一个 put，你知道，它想更新两份副本，对吧，让它们保持同步。它正要发送这个 put，但就在把 put 发给第二台服务器之前，它崩溃了，对吧，停电、操作系统有 bug 之类的。所以现在我们留下的状态很遗憾是：我们发出了这个 put，于是更新了其中

cues.en: of the two replicas to have value 21, but the other one's still with 20. Now, if somebody comes along and reads with a get, they want to read the value associated with key one, they might get 21, or they might get 20, depending on who they talk to. And even if the rule is you always talk to the top server first, if you're building a fault tolerance system, the actual rule has to be, oh, you talk to the top server first, unless it's failed, in which case you talk to the bottom server. So either way, someday you risk exposing
cues.zh: 两台副本中的一台，使其值为 21，但另一台仍然是 20。现在，如果有人来用 get 读取，他们想读键 1 对应的值，可能会得到 21，也可能得到 20，取决于他们跟谁通信。而且即使规则是你总是先跟上面那台服务器通信，如果你在构建容错系统，实际规则必须是：哦，你先跟上面那台服务器通信，除非它故障了，这种情况下你就跟下面那台服务器通信。所以无论哪种方式，总有一天你可能暴露出

cues.en: this stale copy of the data to some future get. It could be that many gets get the updated 21 and then like next week all of a sudden some get yields a week old copy of the data. So that's not very consistent. So in order, but it's the kind of thing that could happen. And we're not careful. So we need to have, we need to actually write down.
cues.zh: 这份过期数据副本给未来某个 get。可能很多 get 都拿到更新后的 21，然后比如下周，突然某个 get 返回了一周前的数据副本。所以这不太一致。所以，这个顺序，但这是可能发生的那类事。如果我们不小心，就会这样。所以我们需要，我们需要真正写下来。

cues.en: what the rules are going to be about puts and gets given this danger of due to replication. And it turns out there's many different definitions you can have of consistency. Many of them are relatively straightforward. Many of them sound like, well, a get yields the value put by the most recently completed put. And so that's usually called strong consistency.
cues.zh: 鉴于复制带来的这种风险，关于 put 和 get 的规则会是什么样的。事实证明，一致性的定义有很多种。其中不少都相当直观。很多听起来像是：get 会返回最近一次完成的 put 所写入的值。这通常被称为强一致性。

cues.en: It turns out also, it's very useful to build systems that have much weaker consistency. For example, do not guarantee anything like a get sees the value written by the most recent put. And the reason, so there's, there's strongly consistent systems that usually have some version of get seeing most recent puts. Although you have to, there's a lot of details to work out. There's also weakly consistent, many sort of.
cues.zh: 事实证明，构建一致性弱得多的系统也非常有用。比如，不保证 get 能看到最近一次 put 写入的值。原因是，强一致系统通常都有某种形式的 get 能看到最近的 put。当然，你得把很多细节理清楚。还有弱一致的，很多种。

cues.en: are flavors of weakly consistent systems that do not make any such guarantee. That may guarantee, well, if someone does a put, then you may not see the put. You may see old values that weren't updated by the put for an unbattered amount of time, maybe. And the reason for people being very interested in weak consistency schemes is that strong consistency, that is, having reads actually be guaranteed to see.
cues.zh: 这类系统属于弱一致性系统，不做任何此类保证。也就是说，如果有人执行了一次写入，你可能看不到这次写入。在一段不受限制的时间内，你可能会看到没有被这次写入更新的旧值。人们之所以对弱一致性方案感兴趣，是因为强一致性，也就是保证读取操作确实能够看到……

cues.en: the most recent write, that's a very expensive spec to implement. Because what it means is almost certainly that you have to, somebody has to do a lot of communication in order to actually implement some notion of strong consistency. If you have multiple copies, it means that either the writer or the reader, or maybe both, has to consult every copy. Like in this case,
cues.zh: ……最近一次写入，这是一个实现起来非常昂贵的规范。因为它几乎肯定意味着，你必须——总得有人进行大量的通信，才能真正实现某种意义上的强一致性。如果你有多份副本，那就意味着写方或者读方，也可能两者都，必须查询每一份副本。就像在这个例子里，

cues.en: where maybe a client crash left one updated but not the other. If we wanted to implement strong consistency in maybe a simple way in the system, we'd have readers read both of the copies, or if there's more than one copy, all the copies, and use the most recently written value that they find. But that's expensive. That's a lot of chit chat to read one value. So in order to avoid communication as much as possible,
cues.zh: 比如可能因为客户端崩溃，一个副本更新了而另一个没有。如果我们在系统里想用简单方式实现强一致性，就会让读方读取两个副本；如果副本不止一个，就读取所有副本，并采用找到的最新写入值。但这很昂贵。读一个值要来回通信这么多次。所以为了尽可能避免通信，

cues.en: Particularly if replicas are far away, people build weak systems that might actually allow the stale read of an old value in this case. Although there's often more semantics attached to that to try to make these weak schemes more useful. And where this communication problem, strong consistency requiring expensive communication, where this really runs you into trouble is that if we're using replication for fault tolerance,
cues.zh: 特别是当副本相距很远时，人们会构建一些弱一致性系统，在这种情况下它们实际上可能允许读到旧值的过期数据。不过通常还会附加一些额外的语义，来让这些弱一致性方案更加实用。而这个通信问题——强一致性需要代价高昂的通信——真正让你陷入困境的地方在于，如果我们把复制用于容错，

cues.en: then we really want the replicas to have independent failure probability, to have uncorrelated failure. So for example, putting both of the replicas of our data in the same rack in the same machine room is probably a really bad idea because if someone trips over the power cable to that rack, both of our copies of our data are going to die because they're both attached to the same power cable in the same rack. So in the search for making replicas as
cues.zh: 那我们确实希望副本的故障概率相互独立、故障不相关。比如，把数据的两个副本放在同一机房的同一机架里，可能非常糟糕，因为如果有人绊到那个机架的电源线，两份数据副本都会完蛋，因为它们都接在同一机架的同一条电源线上。所以，在设法让副本尽可能

cues.en: as independent in failure as possible in order to get decent fault tolerance, people would love to put different replicas as far apart as possible, like in different cities or maybe on opposite sides of the continent. So an earthquake that destroys one data center will be extremely unlikely to also destroy the other data center that has the other copy. So we'd love to be able to do that. If you do that, then the other copy is thousands of miles away.
cues.zh: 尽可能做到在故障方面相互独立，以获得良好的容错性，人们会很乐意把不同的副本放得尽可能远，比如放在不同的城市，甚至大陆的两端。这样，一场摧毁某个数据中心的地震，也极不可能同时摧毁存有另一份副本的另一个数据中心。我们很希望能做到这一点。但如果这样做，另一份副本就在几千英里之外了。

cues.en: And the rate at which light travels means that it may take on the order of milliseconds or tens of milliseconds to communicate to a data center across the continent in order to update the other copy of the data. And so that makes the communication required for strong consistency, for good consistency, potentially extremely expensive. Like every time you want to do one of these put operations or maybe a get, depending on how you implement it.
cues.zh: 光的传播速度意味着，要跨越整个大陆与数据中心通信、更新另一份数据副本，可能需要几毫秒甚至几十毫秒。因此，为了实现强一致性，也就是良好的一致性所需的通信，代价可能极其高昂。比如，每次执行一次这样的 put 操作，或者根据实现方式，也可能是 get 操作时。

cues.en: You might have to sit there waiting for like 10 or 20 or 30 milliseconds in order to talk to both copies of the data to ensure that they're both updated or both checked to find the latest copy. And that tremendous expense, right? This is 10 or 20 or 30 milliseconds on machines that, after all, execute a billion instructions per second. So we're wasting a lot of potential instructions while we wait.
cues.zh: 你可能得在那里等上 10、20 甚至 30 毫秒，才能同时访问两份数据副本，确保它们都已更新，或者都已检查过，从而找到最新的副本。这代价太高了，对吧？毕竟，机器每秒能执行十亿条指令，这可是 10、20 或 30 毫秒。所以等待期间，我们浪费了大量本可以执行的指令。

cues.en: People often build much weaker systems. You're allowed to only update the nearest copy or only consult the nearest copy. I mean, there's a huge sort of amount of academic and real world research on how to structure weak consistency guarantees so they're actually useful to applications and how to take advantage of them in order to actually get high performance. All right, so that's a lightning preview of the technical ideas in the course.

cues.zh: 我要运行键 A 的 reduce 了，请查看你磁盘上存储的中间 map 输出，把所有键 A 的实例挑出来，通过网络发给我。于是 reduce 的 worker 就会这么做，它会从每个 worker 那里获取所有它负责的键的实例——master 告诉它负责哪些键。等收集完所有这些数据，它就可以调用 reduce 了。reduce 函数自身会调用 reduce 的 emit，

cues.en: different from the map emit. And what reduces emit does is writes the output to a file in a cluster file service that Google uses. So here's something I haven't mentioned. I haven't mentioned where the input lives and where the output lives. They're both files. Because any piece of input, we want the flexibility
cues.zh: 它和 map 的 emit 不一样。reduce 的 emit 做的是把输出写到 Google 使用的一个集群文件服务的文件里。这里有个我还没提到的点：输入存放在哪里，输出又存放在哪里。它们都是文件。因为任何一份输入，我们都希望有灵活性，

cues.en: to be able to read any piece of input on any worker server, that means we need some kind of network file system to store the input data. And so indeed, the paper talks about this thing called GFS for Google File System. And GFS is a cluster file system, and GFS actually runs on exactly the same set of workers that worker servers that run MapReduce.
cues.zh: 能在任何一台 worker 服务器上读取任何一份输入，这就意味着我们需要某种网络文件系统来存储输入数据。确实，论文讲到了这个叫 GFS 的东西，即 Google 文件系统。GFS 是一个集群文件系统，而且 GFS 实际上运行在和运行 MapReduce 的那批 worker 服务器完全相同的一组机器上。

cues.en: The input, GFS just automatically, when you, you know, it's a file system, you can read and write files, it just automatically splits up any big file you store on it across lots of servers in 64 megabyte chunks. So if you write, you know, if you have 10 terabytes of crawled web page contents, and you just write them to GFS, even as a single big file, GFS will automatically split that vast amount of data up into 64 kilobyte chunks distributed evenly over...
cues.zh: 输入方面，GFS 会自动——你知道，它是个文件系统，你可以读写文件——它会把存进去的任何大文件自动切成 64 MB 的块，分散到很多服务器上。所以如果你写入，比如你有 10 TB 抓取到的网页内容，直接写进 GFS，哪怕作为单个大文件，GFS 也会自动把这么海量的数据切成 64 KB 的块，均匀分布到……

cues.en: all of the GFS servers, which is to say, all the servers that Google has available. And that's fantastic. That's just what we need. If we then want to run a MapReduce job that takes the entire crawled web as input, the data is already stored in a way that's split up evenly across all the servers. And so that means that the map workers, we're going to launch, if we have 1,000 servers, we're going to launch 1,000 map workers, each reading one 1,000 of the input data.
cues.zh: ……所有 GFS 服务器上，也就是说，分布到 Google 所有可用服务器上。这太棒了，这正是我们需要的。然后如果我们想跑一个 MapReduce 作业，把整个抓取网页作为输入，数据已经以均匀分散在所有服务器上的方式存好了。这意味着，我们要启动的 map worker——如果有 1000 台服务器，就启动 1000 个 map worker，每个读取输入数据的一千分之一。

cues.en: And they're going to be able to read the data in parallel from 1,000 GFS file servers, thus getting tremendous total read throughput, the read throughput of 1,000 servers. So are you thinking maybe that Google has one set of physical machines that run GFS and a separate set of physical machines that run MapReduce jobs? So the question is, what is this arrow here?
cues.zh: 它们就能从 1000 台 GFS 文件服务器并行读取数据，从而获得巨大的总读取吞吐量，相当于 1000 台服务器的读取吞吐量。那么你是不是在想，Google 可能有一组物理机跑 GFS，另有一组独立的物理机跑 MapReduce 作业？所以问题是，这里的箭头是什么？

cues.en: And the answer to that actually sort of changed over the years as Google's involved the system. But in the most general case, if we have big files stored in some big network file system, like GFS is a bit like AFS you might have used on Athena, where you go talk to some collection and your data is split over big collection of servers. You have to go talk to those servers over the network to retrieve your data.
cues.zh: 这个问题的答案，其实随着这些年 Google 系统的发展有所变化。但在最一般的情况下，如果我们把大文件存在某种大型网络文件系统里，比如 GFS 有点像你可能在 Athena 上用过的 AFS：你去和某个集合通信，而你的数据分散在一大组服务器上。你必须通过网络和那些服务器通信，才能取回数据。

cues.en: In that case, what this arrow might represent is the MapReduce worker process has to go off and talk across the network to the correct GFS server or maybe servers that store its part of the input and fetch it over the network to the MapReduce worker machine in order to pass the map. And that's certainly the most general case. And that was eventually how MapReduce actually worked. In the world of this paper though,
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，这个箭头可能表示：MapReduce worker 进程必须通过网络去和正确的 GFS 服务器——或者存有它那部分输入的多个服务器——通信，再通过网络把数据取到 MapReduce worker 所在的机器上，以便执行 map。这当然是最一般的情况，后来 MapReduce 实际也是这样工作的。不过在这篇论文所处的环境里，

cues.en: And, and, and if you did that, that's a lot of network communication. When you're talking about 10 terabytes of data, now we have to move 10 terabytes across their data center network, which, you know, data center networks run at gigabits per second, but it's still a lot of time to move tens of terabytes of data. In order to try to, and indeed in the world of this paper in 2004, the most constraining bottleneck in their MapReduce system was network throughput. Because they were running on a network, if you sort of read as far as the.
cues.zh: 而且，而且，如果你这么做，那会产生大量网络通信。当你说的是 10 TB 数据时，现在得把 10 TB 数据搬过他们的数据中心网络；你知道，数据中心网络跑在每秒千兆位上，但搬几十 TB 数据仍然要花很多时间。为了尝试……而事实上，在这篇论文所处的 2004 年的环境里，他们 MapReduce 系统中最受限的瓶颈是网络吞吐量。因为他们运行在网络上，如果你继续往下读……

cues.en: evaluation section. Their network, their network was, they had thousands of machines, whatever, and they would collect machines, they would plug machines into, you know, each rack of machines into, you know, an Ethernet switch for that rack or something. But then, you know, they all need to talk to each other. But there was a root Ethernet switch that all of the rack Ethernet switches talked to. And this, and
cues.zh: 评估部分。他们的网络，他们的网络是这样的：他们有成千上万台机器之类的设备，会把机器集中起来，然后把每个机架里的机器接入该机架对应的以太网交换机。但这些机器都需要彼此通信。所有机架的以太网交换机还要连接到一个根以太网交换机。这个交换机还……

cues.en: So if you just pick some MapReduce worker and some GFS server, chances are at least half the time the communication between them has to pass through this one route switch. Their route switch had only some amount of total throughput, which I forget. Some number of gigabits per second. Anyway, I forget the number. But when I did the division, that is divided up the...
cues.zh: 所以，假设你随便选一个 MapReduce worker 和一个 GFS server，它们之间的通信至少有一半时间可能都要经过这个根交换机。他们的根交换机总吞吐量有限，具体数值我忘了，大概是每秒若干吉比特。总之我记不清了。但我用总吞吐量除以……

cues.en: Total throughput available in the root switch by the roughly 2,000 servers that they used in the paper's experiments. What I got was that each machine's share of the root switch, or of the total network capacity, was only 50 megabits per second in their setup. So 50 megabits per second per machine. And that might seem like a lot 50 megabits. Gosh, millions and millions. But it's actually quite small compared to how fast, say, disks run or.
cues.zh: 论文实验中使用的大约 2,000 台服务器后，得到的结果是：在他们的配置中，每台机器能分到的根交换机带宽，也就是总网络容量的份额，只有每秒 50 兆比特。每台机器每秒 50 兆比特。50 兆比特听起来似乎已经很多了，毕竟是几百万比特。但和磁盘的运行速度相比，这其实相当低，或者说……

cues.en: CPUs run. And so this, with their network, this 50 megabits per second was like a tremendous limit. And so they really stood on their heads in the design described in the paper to avoid using the network. And they played a bunch of tricks to avoid sending stuff over the network when they possibly could avoid it. One of them was they ran the GFS servers and the MapReduce workers on the same set of machines.
cues.zh: 和 CPU 的运行速度相比也是如此。所以在他们的网络中，每秒 50 兆比特构成了巨大的限制。因此，论文描述的设计极力避免使用网络。他们想尽各种办法，只要能不通过网络发送数据，就尽量不发送。其中一个办法是让 GFS server 和 MapReduce worker 运行在同一组机器上。

cues.en: so that they have a thousand machines, they'd run GFS, they'd implement their GFS service on that thousand machines and run MapReduce on the same thousand machines. And then when the master was splitting up the map work and sort of farming it out to different workers, it would cleverly, when it was about to run the map that was going to read from input file one, it would figure out from GFS which server
cues.zh: 也就是说，假设他们有 1,000 台机器，就在这 1,000 台机器上实现 GFS 服务，同时在同一批机器上运行 MapReduce。当 master 把 map 任务拆分并分发给不同 worker 时，如果它准备运行一个要读取输入文件 1 的 map，就会聪明地先从 GFS 查询哪个 server 的本地磁盘上……

cues.en: actually holds input file one on its local disk. And it would send the map for that input file to the MapReduce software on the same machine. So that by default, this arrow was actually local read from the local disk and did not involve the network. And depending on failures or load or whatever, it couldn't always do that. But almost all of the maps would be run on the very same machine that stored the data, thus saving them.
cues.zh: 实际存储着输入文件 1，然后把这个输入文件对应的 map 发送给同一台机器上的 MapReduce 软件。这样一来，默认情况下，这条箭头表示的其实是从本地磁盘进行本地读取，完全不需要网络。由于故障、负载等原因，这种安排不一定总能实现。但几乎所有 map 都会在存储数据的同一台机器上运行，从而节省了……

cues.en: vast amount of time that they would otherwise have to wait to move the input data across the network. The next trick they played is that a map, as I mentioned before, stores its output on the local disk of the machine that you run the map on. So again, storing the output of the map does not require network communication, at least not immediately, because the output's stored on the disk. However, we know for sure that one way or another, in order to group together
cues.zh: 否则就必须等待输入数据通过网络传输所耗费的大量时间。他们采用的第二个技巧是，正如我之前提到的，map 会把输出存储在运行该 map 的机器的本地磁盘上。因此，存储 map 的输出同样不需要网络通信，至少暂时不需要，因为输出被存储在磁盘上。不过我们确定，无论如何，为了把……

cues.en: All of, you know, by the way the map reduces to find, in order to group together all of the values associated with the given key and pass them to a single invocation of reduce on some machine, this is going to require network communication. We're going to, you know, we want to need to fetch all the A's and give them a single machine to have to be moved across the network. And so this shuffle, this movement of the keys from this kind of
cues.zh: MapReduce 找到的、与某个给定键关联的所有值集中起来，并将它们传给某台机器上 reduce 的一次调用，这必然需要网络通信。比如，我们需要获取所有的 A，并把它们发送到同一台机器上，因此必须通过网络传输。也就是说，这个 shuffle，也就是把键从这种……

cues.en: They're originally stored by row on the same machine that ran the map. We need them essentially to be stored by column on the machine that's going to be responsible for reduce. This transformation of row storage, essentially column storage, the paper calls a shuffle. And really that required moving every piece of data across the network from the map that produced it to the reduce that would need it. And now it's like the expensive part of the map reduce. Yeah.
cues.zh: 它们原本按行存储在运行 map 的同一台机器上，转换为按列存储在负责执行 reduce 的机器上。论文把这种从按行存储到按列存储的转换称为 shuffle。实际上，这要求把每一份数据都通过网络，从生成它的 map 移动到需要它的 reduce。这就是 MapReduce 中代价高昂的部分。对。

cues.en: You can imagine a different definition in which you have a more kind of streaming reduce. I don't know, I haven't thought this through, I don't know why, whether that would be feasible or not. Certainly as far as programmer interface, like if the goal, their number one goal really was to be able to make it easy to program by people who just had no idea what was going on in the system. So it may be that this spec, this is really the way reduce functions look.
cues.zh: 你可以想象另一种定义，用一种更像是流式的归约。我也说不好，我没仔细想过，不知道那到底可不可行。不过从程序员接口的角度来说，毕竟他们的首要目标，就是让那些完全不了解系统内部运作的人也能轻松编程。所以也许这个规范，这确实是归约函数应有的样子。

cues.en: in C++ or something. Like a streaming version of this is now starting to look, I don't know how it would look. Probably not this simple. But you know, maybe it could be done that way. And indeed, many modern systems. And people have gotten a lot more sophisticated with modern things that are the successors to MapReduce. And they do indeed involve processing streams of data often rather than this very batch approach. This is a batch approach in the sense that
cues.zh: 比如用 C++ 之类的语言实现。流式版本会是什么样，我不知道它会是什么样子。可能不会这么简单。但也许可以那样实现。事实上，很多现代系统，人们在 MapReduce 的各种后继系统上已经做得精细多了。这些系统往往确实采用流式数据处理，而不是这种非常批处理的 approach。说它是批处理，是因为

cues.en: We wait until we get all the data, and then we process it. So first of all, you then have to have a notion of finite inputs. Modern systems often do indeed use streams and are able to take advantage of some efficiencies due to that, but not MapReduce. OK, so this is the point at which the shuffle is where all the network traffic happens. This can actually be a vast amount of data. So if you think about sort.
cues.zh: 我们要等拿到全部数据之后才开始处理。所以首先，你得有有限输入的概念。现代系统确实经常使用流，并能借此获得一些效率上的优势，但 MapReduce 不是这样。好，接下来就到了 shuffle 这一阶段，所有网络流量都发生在这里。这里的数据量可能非常庞大。以 sort 为例。

cues.en: If you're sorting, the, the output of the sort has the same size as the input to the sort. So that means that if you're, you know, if your input is 10 terabytes of data and you're running a sort, you're moving 10 terabytes of data across the network at this point. And your output will also be 10 terabytes. And so this is quite a lot of data. And indeed it is for many MapReduce jobs. Although not all, there's some that significantly reduce the amount of data at these stages.
cues.zh: 排序时，排序的输出和输入的大小是一样的。也就是说，如果你的输入是 10 TB 的数据，运行一个 sort 任务，那在这一步你就要在网络上传输 10 TB 的数据。而你的输出同样也是 10 TB。这数据量相当大。对很多 MapReduce 作业来说确实如此，虽然不是全部，也有一些作业在这些阶段会显著减少数据量。

cues.en: Somebody mentioned, oh, what if you want to feed the output of reduce into another MapReduce job? And indeed, that was often what people wanted to do. And in any case, the output of the reduce might be enormous, like for sort or web indexing. The output of the reduce is on 10 terabytes of input. The output of the reduce is, again, going to be 10 terabytes. So the output of the reduce was also stored on GFS. And the system would, you know, reduce would just produce these key value pairs, but the MapReduce framework would gather them up.
cues.zh: 有人提到，如果把 reduce 的输出再喂给另一个 MapReduce 作业会怎样？事实上，人们经常就是这么做的。而且无论如何，reduce 的输出可能非常庞大，比如 sort 或网页索引。在 10 TB 的输入上，reduce 的输出同样会是 10 TB。所以 reduce 的输出也存储在 GFS 上。系统呢，reduce 本身只是产生这些键值对，但 MapReduce 框架会把它们收集起来，

cues.en: and write them into giant files on GFS. And so there was another round of network communication required to get the output of each reduce to the GFS server that needed to store that reduce. And because you might think that they could have played the same trick with the output of storing the output on the GFS server that happened to run the MapReduce worker that ran the reduce.
cues.zh: 写入 GFS 上的巨型文件。因此还需要再一轮网络通信，把每个 reduce 的输出送到需要存储它的 GFS 服务器上。你可能会想，他们本可以耍同样的花招——把输出直接存在恰好运行了执行该 reduce 的 MapReduce worker 的那台 GFS 服务器上。

cues.en: And maybe they did do that, but because GFS as well as splitting data out for performance also keeps two or three copies for fault tolerance. That means no matter what you need to write one copy of the data across a network to a different server. So there's a lot of network communication here and a bunch here also. And it was this network communication that really limited the throughput of MapReduce in 2004. In 2020, because this network arrangement was
cues.zh: 也许他们确实这么做了，但 GFS 除了为性能拆分数据外，还会保留两到三份副本用于容错。这意味着无论如何，你都需要通过网络把一份数据写到另一台服务器上。所以这里有很多网络通信，这里也有一大堆。正是这种网络通信，真正限制了 2004 年 MapReduce 的吞吐量。到了 2020 年，因为这种网络布局

cues.en: such a limiting factor for so many things people wanted to do in data centers. Modern data center networks are a lot faster at the root than this was. And so one typical data center network you might see today actually has many root, instead of a single root switch that everything has to go through, you might have many root switches and each rack switch has a connection to each of these sort of replicated root switches and the traffic is split up among the root switches. So modern data center networks.
cues.zh: 对人们在数据中心想做的许多事情来说，成了如此大的限制因素。现代数据中心网络在根交换机层面比这快得多。所以今天你可能看到的一个典型数据中心网络，实际上有许多根交换机；不再是所有流量都必须经过的单一根交换机，而是可能有许多根交换机，每个机架交换机都连接到这些冗余根交换机中的每一个，流量则分散到各根交换机之间。所以现代数据中心网络

cues.en: have far more network throughput. And because of that, actually modern, I think Google sort of stopped using MapReduce a few years ago, but before they stopped using it, the modern MapReduce actually no longer tried to run the maps on the same machine as the data was stored on. They were happy to load the data from anywhere because they just assumed the network was extremely fast. Okay, we're out of time for MapReduce.
cues.zh: 拥有高得多的网络吞吐量。也正因如此，其实我觉得 Google 几年前就有点停用 MapReduce 了；但在停用之前，现代 MapReduce 实际上已不再尝试把 map 任务运行在存储数据的同一台机器上。他们乐于从任何地方加载数据，因为他们直接假定网络极快。好，MapReduce 我们就讲到这儿。
